    Tesla (TSLA): the car pays, the close assumes a mile

    Tesla's Q2 sales gross profit was $6,645 per cash delivery. The Oct 2 close assumes a paid driverless mile that is not in the accounts. Research only.

    Research only. Not financial advice.

    Tesla sells two things that show up in the accounts: a finished electric vehicle, and a kilowatt-hour of storage. The car still pays the bills. Storage is the second engine. The Oct 2 close is priced as if a third thing, a paid driverless mile, were already the product.

    The number to remember is $6,645. That is automotive sales gross profit per cash delivery in the second quarter of 2026. Price $42,337, cost $35,692, profit $6,645, before operating expenses and before the $12,057 of company capex that landed in the same quarter for every vehicle delivered. Derived from the Q2 2026 update exhibit. Cash deliveries are total deliveries minus deliveries subject to operating lease accounting, which is the company's own denominator for average cost per vehicle.

    Research view

    The Oct 2 close already assumes a paid driverless mile that is not in the accounts. Under the stated model, we see more downside than upside.

    Medium conviction. The model window is 12 months, with a read of the Oct 21, 2026 print. This is a research view. It is not an instruction.

    Reference print: $370.59, MarketBeat closing price, 16:00 ET, Friday Oct 2, 2026. Markets were closed Oct 3 and Oct 4. One close, in prose. No price series is filed with this note. StockAnalysis history, read 20:03 ET Oct 4, shows that same Oct 2 close at $370.59, up 4.65% on the day. One day. No series is republished. Deliveries that day were 486,532, from the Oct 2 8-K. CnEVPost, read 20:03 ET Oct 4, says those deliveries were about 4.91% above a 463,761 consensus. The beat is already in the reference print.

    One share count for the equity value: 3,949,547,394 shares outstanding as of July 16, 2026, Form 10-Q cover. No share count as of Oct 2 was in the saved filings. The date mismatch is stated.

    Equity value: 3,949,547,394 times $370.59 is $1.464 trillion. Derived. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments at June 30, 2026: $43,524 million, Q2 update. Aggregate principal of indebtedness at June 30, 2026: $9.08 billion, of which $1.35 billion was current, Form 10-Q. Net cash $34.444 billion. Enterprise value about $1.429 trillion. Both derived. The Sept 29 facilities are undrawn and are not in this net cash figure.

    What the accounts show

    The car and the pack are a real hardware business. Cost per cash delivery did not fall across the five quarters in the Q2 update. Regulatory credits fell. Capex in the latest quarter was larger than sales gross profit per car. Trailing operating income is $4.4 billion. The close is not paying for the car.

    QuarterCash deliveriesSales GP per carCost per car
    2025 Q2377,452$5,882$35,944
    2025 Q3486,869$6,150$35,667
    2025 Q4407,231$7,062$34,069
    2026 Q1354,593$8,057$35,579
    2026 Q2472,546$6,645$35,692

    ASP is automotive sales revenue divided by cash deliveries. Q2 automotive sales were $20,006 million. 472,546 times $42,336.62 equals $20,006 million. The gap versus reported automotive sales is zero, by construction. Leasing revenue is a separate line ($364 million in Q2) and is not in the ASP.

    Q2 automotive sales cost was $16,866 million. Sales gross profit was $3,140 million, or 15.7% of automotive sales. That ratio is not the company's automotive gross margin. Credits and leasing sit on other lines.

    Regulatory credits in Q2 were $146 million, against $439 million a year earlier on the same update table. Per delivery that is $304, against $1,143 a year earlier. Credits are not a durable unit of profit.

    Energy is a proxy, not a clean unit price. Segment revenue includes generation, storage sales, and leasing. Deployments were 13.5 GWh in Q2. $3,139 million divided by 13.5 million kWh is $233 per kWh. Gross profit was $640 million, or $47 per kWh. The 10-Q says energy gross margin fell from 30.3% to 20.4% year over year, on a lower average selling price per Megapack, fewer Powerwall deployments, and a higher cost per MWh. The proxy will not match a pure Megapack list. That list was not in the saved filings. The $47 per kWh proxy, and the second-engine line above, need a related-party flag. The June 30, 2026 Form 10-Q, Note 13, books $318 million of Q2 revenue and $242 million of cost from SpaceX Megapack purchases. That is 10.1% of Q2 energy revenue of $3,139 million. Gross profit on those sales was $76 million, or 23.9%, against 20.4% for the energy segment. Derived from the 10-Q and the Q2 update. The same person is CEO of Tesla and of SpaceX. A CEO-affiliated buyer is a large storage customer. The proxy is not a clean third-party unit price.

    Cost per cash delivery ran from $34,069 to $35,944 across five quarters. It did not fall. No company unit-cost claim is drawn on the chart.

    Q2 2026, from the update: revenue $28,236 million, gross profit $4,751 million, operating income $398 million, net income to common stockholders $1,114 million. Operating margin was 1.4%, against 4.1% a year earlier, on the same financial-summary line. That net income includes a $1,005 million unrealized gain on the SpaceX stake. Without that gain, net income to common is about $109 million. Derived. The gain is about 90% of the reported net income to common. Operating income is the cleaner figure. Research and development was $2,371 million, against $1,589 million a year earlier. Stock-based compensation in the cash-flow statement was $1,151 million, against $635 million a year earlier. Both from the Q2 update. Operating cash flow $4,697 million. Capex $5,789 million, up 142% from $2,394 million a year earlier, on the same summary line. Free cash flow negative $1,092 million.

    Trailing twelve months, sum of the update columns from 2025 Q3 through 2026 Q2: operating income $4,372 million, net income to common $3,804 million, revenue $103,619 million. The update's own trailing capex column is $12,923 million and trailing operating cash flow is $18,685 million, so trailing free cash flow is $5,762 million. One bad quarter is not the year. The year still funded a $5.8 billion quarter of capex that the quarter's operations did not cover.

    Capex per delivery in Q2: $5,789 million divided by 480,126 deliveries is $12,057. That is company capex, not a vehicle bill of materials. Lifetime sales gross profit on one car at the Q2 rate, if the car is never sold again, is $6,645. The quarter spent more capex per car than the car returned in sales gross profit.

    Services gross profit in Q2 was $648 million on $4,581 million of revenue. Real, and still smaller than the car.

    FSD subscriptions: 1.48 million active at quarter end, up from 0.95 million a year earlier on the same table. The company said over 55% of new North American deliveries included an FSD subscription. Subscription price is not in the saved text. Deferred revenue related to connectivity, FSD (Supervised), free Supercharging and software updates was $4.05 billion at June 30, 2026, versus $3.87 billion at Dec 31, 2025. That stock is about $1,026 per cover share. It is not a robotaxi business.

    Drivers

    Four drivers carry the view.

    1. The unit. Gross profit per cash car is about $6,645. Volume is not the fragile input. A $2,000 cost miss on the Q2 cash-delivery count wipes about $0.95 billion of sales gross profit at constant volume. Cost and price move the unit. Volume does not, inside the range we checked.
    1. The mile is not a line. Paid autonomous miles are not in the 10-Q revenue table. The Q2 update draws cumulative paid robotaxi miles on a chart and does not print the number in the HTML text. Company statements outside that filing text are small. Business Insider, reporting the Q2 call, says Tesla put cumulative paid miles at nearly 2.5 million by the end of Q2, and that figure includes trips with a safety monitor. Electrek, Sep 3, 2026, reports Tesla's announcement of 1 million unsupervised miles. Cite both as company statements, not as a filing line. Against 69 billion to 688 billion miles a year in the requirement table below, 2.5 million cumulative paid miles is about 1/27,600 of the low end of that annual range. The statements make the gap larger, not smaller.
    1. The close needs a different business. At a 20x multiple, which is an assumption with a stated range of 10x to 40x, the $1.464 trillion equity needs about $73.2 billion of earnings. Trailing operating income is $4.37 billion. The gap is about 17 times. That gap is the robotaxi and Optimus option. Those are company timing claims. They are not revenue lines. The Oct 2 delivery print was already public. The Oct 21 financials are not out.
    1. The quarter spent the gross profit. Q2 free cash flow was negative $1,092 million. Trailing free cash flow was still positive. The binding quarter was not the year. It is still the freshest cash print.

    Year-over-year deliveries: 486,532 against 497,099 is negative 2.1%. At Tesla's own latest year-over-year delivery rate, a volume gap versus a rival who is already ahead does not close.

    BYD passenger battery-electric sales in Q3 2026 were 762,478, as reported by CnEVPost's compilation of company reports. That is one compiler. It is not a BYD filing in this folder. Gap versus Tesla on that reported count: 275,946 vehicles. The September BYD sales notice, a company PDF, shows September passenger new-energy sales of 456,713, of which 273,143 were pure electric, and September exports of 180,700. The quarterly pure-electric total is not in that one monthly notice. Treat 762,478 as single-source and reported, not as a two-source fact.

    Storage peers were not saved as primary deployment tables. Not invented.

    What the close implies

Discounting a cash flow that does not exist would make the required future earnings larger, not smaller. The table uses the undiscounted requirement so the gap is a minimum.

    Stated floors in the Q2 update: California above 550,000, Shanghai above 950,000, Berlin above 375,000, Texas Model Y above 250,000, Cybertruck above 125,000, Cybercab above 125,000. Sum of floors above 2.375 million a year. Q2 production of 451,758 annualizes to about 1.81 million, about 76% of that sum. Floors are greater-than, so used share of true capacity is lower.     Superchargers at June 30, 2026: 8,704 stations, 82,357 connectors, connectors up 17% year over year. California TCP permit number TCP0046782-A is the company's citation for supervised Bay Area work. A permit is a lease, not a deed.

    NHTSA opened Audit Query AQ26002 on Sep 3, 2026, on Cybercab FMVSS certification. That is the agency's opening resume, read 20:03 ET Oct 4. A secondary tracker, thechargeport.com, also read 20:03 ET Oct 4, says the query was escalated to a Special Order with sworn answers due Sep 30. That escalation is not in the opening resume. Unverified against NHTSA. It does not carry a conclusion in this note.

    Share count

    Cover shares, July 16, 2026: 3,949,547,394. Basic weighted-average shares, Q2 2026: 3,237 million. Diluted: 3,540 million. Check: $1,114 million divided by 3,237 million is $0.34, and basic EPS is $0.34. The EPS math is internally consistent.

    The legal count and the EPS count differ by about 712 million shares. The 10-Q does not publish a one-line bridge. Inference, not a filing table: 423.7 million unearned 2025 award shares plus about 286.5 million net shares from the Q2 option exercise (about 304.0 million exercised, about 17.5 million net settled) equal about 710 million. If that inference is right, a large block is legally outstanding and not in basic EPS because it is unearned or unvested. Equity value in this note uses the legal count, because that is the claim on the company.

    Path: 3,751 million at Dec 31, 2025, 3,755 million at March 31, 2026, 3,949 million at June 30, 2026. The Q2 jump is mostly the option exercise, not a primary offering. Current beneficial ownership after the exercise was not in a parsed Form 4 in the working file. Gap.

    The 2025 award, from the DEF 14A filed 2025-09-17: 423,743,904 shares, 12 tranches of 35,311,992. Earned only if milestones are met. Not a current share issuance.

    Capital and the related stake

    In the first half of 2026 the company spent $8,282 million on property and equipment and $2,002 million on SpaceX common stock. Q2 stock-based compensation was part of a half-year total of $2,181 million. The Sept 29, 2026 8-K describes a $20.0 billion delayed-draw term loan, an $8.0 billion five-year revolver, and a $2.0 billion 364-day revolver. That is $30 billion of new facilities. No loans were outstanding under those facilities as of Sept 29, 2026. The company does not currently plan to draw in 2026. Liquidity covenant: at least $5.0 billion. The facilities are undrawn.

    Reported, from the June 30, 2026 Form 10-Q, not from a private-company data vendor: Tesla invested $2.00 billion in SpaceX common stock in March 2026, formerly a preferred share investment in xAI, ownership under 1%. Fair value $3,007 million at June 30, 2026, with a $1,005 million unrealized gain in the quarter. Level 2. The 10-Q ties a $238 million discount for lack of marketability to regulatory restrictions expiring in September 2026. Separate from that discount, customary sales restrictions in connection with a SpaceX initial public offering expire in December 2026. The same person is CEO of Tesla and of SpaceX. Those figures are the issuer's reported numbers. They are not an estimate by this desk.

    The Q3 mark will use the quarter-end method, not a straight close-to-close. StockAnalysis history, read 20:03 ET Oct 4, shows one Sep 30 close for SPCX of $150.86. One prose close. No series is republished. The June 30 SPCX close was not used here. The sign and size of the Q3 gain are unknown.

    The 2018 award was exercised in the quarter as described above. The implementation agreement requires continuous service as CEO or as an executive officer for product or operations through Jan 19, 2028. Succession is not disclosed.

    The geometric 12-month outcome sits about 20% below the Oct 2 close. That is why the research view sees more downside than upside. It does not make that equity value an offer. The reference print is where the bull case sits. The evidence in hand is the base.

    What would change the outcomes: a Q3 update that prints robotaxi gross profit, or credits near zero with another energy-margin decline. Not a delivery beat. That already happened, and it is already in the Oct 2 reference print.

    What the Q3 10-Q would have to show

    Oct 21, 2026 is the scheduled print. This is the measurement, not an instruction. Each line below is what would have to be on the page to move the research view. A delivery count alone will not do it. That beat is already in the reference print.

    • Cash deliveries. The Oct 2 exhibit prints 486,532 deliveries and "1%" subject to operating lease accounting. It does not print the cash-delivery count. One percent of 486,532 is not an integer, so the exact count is unknown. To move the view, the 10-Q or the update would have to print cash deliveries and an automotive sales gross profit per cash car that breaks the $6,645 unit by enough to matter against the $73.2 billion earnings requirement at the assumed 20x. A higher delivery count with the same unit does not move the view.
    • SpaceX mark, on the Other income line. Q2's unrealized gain was $1,005 million, about 90% of net income to common, leaving about $109 million without it. A Q3 Other income line that again exceeds Q2 operating income of $398 million would mean the bottom line is still the mark. A line near zero, with operating margin still near 1.4% and no mile disclosure, removes that cushion and leaves the cautious view in place. The Sep 30 SPCX close of $150.86, StockAnalysis, read 20:03 ET Oct 4, does not settle the sign or the size. The June 30 close was not used, and the mark is Level 2, including the marketability discount.
    • Paid miles and unsupervised miles. Company statements in hand are nearly 2.5 million cumulative paid miles at the end of Q2, including safety-monitor trips, and 1 million unsupervised miles announced Sep 3. To move the view, the filing would have to print a paid-mile figure with a denominator that is not a rounding error against 69 billion to 688 billion miles a year.
    • Cybercab fleet size. Not in the filings saved here. One secondary source, Not a Tesla App, read 20:03 ET Oct 4, says 169 Cybercabs were registered in Austin. That is a registration count from a secondary page, not a Tesla disclosure, and not cars confirmed in service. To move the view, the 10-Q would have to print a fleet size.
    • Cover count. The July 16 cover count and the Q2 basic share count differ by about 712 million. The inference that this is the unearned award block is not a filing table. A Q3 cover count still near 3.95 billion makes that branch more likely. A jump of hundreds of millions makes dilution additive. That is the bar for this line.
    • R&D and SBC. Q2 R&D was $2,371 million, against $1,589 million a year earlier. Quarterly SBC was $1,151 million. Both sit inside the 1.4% operating margin. To move the view, these lines would have to fall enough to lift operating margin without a one-time mark. Confirming them near the Q2 levels leaves the view where it is.

    What would change the view

    • Oct 21, 2026. Automotive gross margin excluding credits above 16%, and energy margin back above 25%: the base holds. Credits under $100 million and energy margin under 18%: the bear path.
    • A paid-mile number with a denominator, in the update or the 10-Q: the bull path opens. A chart without a number does not count. The Q2 chart did not count.
    • A draw on the facilities in 2026: contradicts the Sept 29 sentence. Treat it as a cash signpost.
    • Optimus units sold to a third party, disclosed: an option, not a reason to rerate the car.
    • Share count on the Q3 10-Q cover. If it is still about 3.95 billion, the award-shares-already-included branch is more likely. If it jumps by hundreds of millions, dilution is additive.

    A kill of the cautious view is a filing that shows robotaxi gross profit large enough to matter next to the $3.1 billion quarterly car gross profit. A kill of a long view, were one on the table, would be credits near zero, energy margin still near 20%, and capex still above operating cash flow, with no mile disclosure. No trade is on the table.

    Analogy, without a price path

    Cisco in 2000 is the negative analogy: a real product, and a multiple that assumed peak growth would stay. The investor price path is not republished. It came from a price series, and this note does not ship price series. Toyota is the build some readers want this to be. It does not fit. Tesla's last five quarters did not show a falling cost per car, and the equity multiple is not a car multiple. No Toyota cost series was saved, so a cost-down story is not used as a measured fact.

    Gaps

    • Q3 2026 financials. Not filed. Release set for Oct 21, 2026. Every margin and cash figure here stops at June 30, except the Q3 operating counts in the Oct 2 exhibit.
    • Paid robotaxi miles and fleet size. Not printed in the filing text. Company statements and one secondary registration count are in the Oct 21 section above. They are not a filing line.
    • Optimus units deployed and a bill of materials. Not disclosed. No proxy invented.
    • China revenue dollars. Not extracted as a clean table. Shanghai capacity is not a share.
    • Storage peer deployments. Not saved.
    • Current top holders and post-exercise beneficial ownership. Not in a parsed Form 4 here.
    • FSD subscription price. Count saved. Price not in the text.
    • Life-of-asset post census. Not done. No X-only claim carries a conclusion in this note.

    Method

    Run rates: a quarter times four is labeled annualized and is not a forecast. Trailing twelve months is the sum of the Q2 update columns from 2025 Q3 through 2026 Q2.

    ASP and cost per vehicle: automotive sales, or automotive sales cost, divided by deliveries excluding operating-lease deliveries.

    Equity value: one share count (July 16 cover) times one prose close (Oct 2, MarketBeat, 16:00 ET). Enterprise value subtracts June 30 cash and short-term investments and June 30 debt principal. Undrawn facilities are not debt outstanding.

    Charts are drawn from those filing lines and from the labeled assumptions above. Script: data/2026-10-04-tesla/scripts/derive.py. No price series, no price file, and no vendor price library is an input. Model outcomes in this note are percent moves from the Oct 2 close, and equity value at the July 16 cover count. They are labelled model outcomes. They are not offers.

    Desk position: none. No trades, orders, or posts were made for this work.

    Research only. Not financial advice. Nothing here is an offer to buy, sell or hold any asset.
